title: Bonus coins are temporary
body: Just when I thought I had enough coins to open one of the really expensive coin chapters at the end of the book, a bunch of them expired. With how many coins we can earn in a day I don’t believe I can finish the book I’m reading because the bonus coins expire too fast. Though I believe they shouldn’t expire at all. I’ll try for a bit more to see if I can read the last few chapters. I won’t buy coins because that makes the book just too expensive. The $9.99 option only gives you 3-4 chapters and you need 2-3 purchases to finish the book. I will be deleting this application regardless because all books have this last x chapters at an inflated coin cost. I hope I can finish the book before then but I feeling I’m in an endless loop of expiring coins. Given this issue I can’t recommend this application even though the book was good.

Second improvement needed is that when I click an X to exit and add I am not rerouted to a website or the App Store for said ad. Close the damn ad and send me back to my current app.

title: I really hope this is AI
body: I really hope these stories are written by AI, because if these are the result of people’s efforts that’s just depressing. Stories are repetitive and rewrite/contradict themselves all the time, like calling off a trip to London and then being on the plane to London in the next chapter with no acknowledgement. Things like that happen multiple times in each story I’ve read, where the AI or the author doesn’t check their notes or what they’ve already written and just decide someone is now right handed despite the fact they broke their left hand a few chapters ago being significant cause they’re left handed. Chapters are very short to wring all the coins they can out of you, and the ability to watch ads to continue disappears after a certain amount of reading or time in the app.

title: Great Book, But Not Worth the Price
body: This book has a compelling storyline that keeps you hooked and eager to move through each chapter. The chapters are very short and written at about a second-grade reading level, but the content itself is quite mature. It falls into the romance genre and includes explicit, sexual scenes that contrast with the simplicity of the writing style. However, this will be the last book I read on this app because of how expensive it is to continue. Accessing just a small number of very short chapters requires a significant cost, and finishing the book would end up being far more expensive than purchasing a typical book elsewhere. While there is an option to watch ads for access, it only goes so far before payment becomes unavoidable. If I had known this upfront, I wouldn’t have started the book. If the pricing were more reasonable, I would easily rate the app five stars.

body: WeRead is a solid reading app with a large selection of stories, especially for fans of romance and web novels. The interface is clean and easy to navigate, and features like bookmarking, progress tracking, and personalized recommendations make it enjoyable to use. Many users like how simple it is to discover new books and pick up where they left off. ￼ However, the biggest downside is the cost structure. The stories are really good, the few I’ve read anyway it’s just the waiting, especially for someone as adhd as me if I forget or go too long with out unlocking a chapter, I’ll just uninstall and move on.
